title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 159 (Restoration of goods lent gratuitously)

content.overview: Section 159 provides that the lender of a thing for use may at any time require its return, if the loan was gratuitous, even though he lent it for a specified time or purpose. But if, on the faith of such loan made for a specified time or purpose, the borrower has acted in such a manner that the return of the thing lent before the time agreed upon would cause him loss exceeding the benefit actually derived by him from the loan, the lender must, if he compels the return, indemnify the borrower for the amount in which the loss so occasioned exceeds the benefit so derived.
content.glance: Lender of a gratuitous loan may demand return at any time, even if lent for a fixed period or purpose, but must indemnify the borrower for excess loss if early return causes greater loss than benefit derived.

Current-law framing: absolute right to demand return of gratuitous loan, tempered by indemnity for excess reliance loss.

sections.body: The lender of a thing for use may at any time require its return, if the loan was gratuitous, even though he lent it for a specified time or purpose.

sections.heading: Indemnity for excess loss
sections.body: But if, on the faith of such loan made for a specified time or purpose, the borrower has acted in such a manner that the return of the thing lent before the time agreed upon would cause him loss exceeding the benefit actually derived by him from the loan, the lender must, if he compels the return, indemnify the borrower for the amount in which the loss so occasioned exceeds the benefit so derived.

examples.title: Gratuitous loan with reliance
examples.body: A lends a machine free for six months. B incurs expenses relying on the period. A demands early return. If loss exceeds benefit, A must indemnify the excess under Section 159.

hypotheticals.question: Lender demands early return of a gratuitous loan after the borrower has acted in reliance. What is the consequence?
hypotheticals.analysis: Lender may demand return, but must indemnify the borrower for excess loss over benefit derived, under Section 159.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 159 allows the lender of a gratuitous loan to require return at any time, even if lent for a specified time or purpose. However, if the borrower has acted in reliance so that early return causes loss exceeding the benefit derived, the lender must indemnify the excess if he compels return.
examples: Early demand of free loan after reliance — indemnity for excess loss.
distinctions: Applies to gratuitous loans for use; distinct from general return duties under Section 160.
